A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiveXiv benchmark and IRT-based evaluation framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison. Numerical inconsistencies in some later tables are identifiable document issues, not missing evidence.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original evaluations of 17 LMMs, manual-subset validation, domain and question-type analyses, and efficient-evaluation experiments, including MM-LiveBench in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains original empirical results and adds evaluations across dataset releases, physics domains, generator/filter configurations, historical papers, and additional manually verified subsets.

M1.justification: The original pipeline uses GPT-4o for generation and Claude for filtering. v3.pdf extends it with rotating assignments involving Qwen2-VL-72B in dataset version 3 and reciprocal GPT-4o/Claude roles in version 4 (Appendices A.4.4 and A.5.3). These are limited procedural adaptations; the extraction, prompting, Rasch estimator, and Fisher-information selection procedure remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from ten scientific domains to fourteen by adding applied physics, biophysics, physics data analysis, and optics. Evaluated releases 2–4 and a historical dataset constructed from 2010 papers add substantial temporal coverage and a distribution-shift scenario. VQA, TQA, and the existing MM-LiveBench experiment are retained.

E2.justification: The original 17-model comparison is retained, while Pixtral and Molmo-7B join the later-release evaluations, producing 19-model comparisons in Tables 13–14 and the longitudinal IRT experiments. No new competing efficient-evaluation algorithm is evaluated.

E3.justification: The main IRT evaluation changes from a chronological split with approximately 85% held out to sequential evaluation across actual LiveXiv releases. Budgets expand from 3, 5, and 8 re-evaluated models to include 12; newly introduced models are outside that budget at release 2. New protocols include generator-role controls and manual checks of 300 questions per task in dataset version 3. Main efficiency plots exclude its Qwen-generated questions, with the full-question experiment reported separately.

E4.justification: New analyses investigate generator/filter role reversal, three-model generation and filtering, temporal shift from 2010 papers, difficulty and content diversity across releases, and additional manual-validation ranking stability. v3.pdf also reports GPT-4o temperature, resolution, and prompt sensitivity checks. The earlier simulated-split budget analyses are replaced by longitudinal studies, and the explicit test-size-versus-error plot is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report IRT prediction MAE with mean absolute deviation and Spearman rank correlations. The additional plots extend the same reporting practice. No new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are supplied; changing 'variance' to 'deviation' in the abstract does not change Table 2's calculations.

E6.justification: Substantial new release-specific, role-reversal, historical-data, and manual-validation results are reported. The earlier simulated-split MAEs of 1.2/2.2 percentage points differ in setting from the later release-4 results of 1.4/2.3, so they do not establish a performance gain or loss. Existing entries also change: Table 5 revises Idefics2's static rank from 12 to 13. Table 1 swaps Qwen2-VL and InternVL2-8B TQA means from 60.2/62.1 to 62.1/60.2, conflicting with the retained assignments in Table 7.

T1.justification: Section 3.3.2 changes the unconditional assumption that the model set grows monotonically into a usual-case statement allowing deprecation. This is a limited formal-assumption refinement; deprecation handling was already discussed operationally. The Rasch formulation, performance estimator, and Fisher-information criterion are otherwise retained, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain automated contamination-resistant benchmarking and efficient evaluation. The introduction strengthens the claimed evaluation reduction from 70% to at least approximately 75%; Section 3.3 additionally emphasizes that three, rather than only five, re-evaluated models can suffice.

C2.justification: The later appendices add substantive interpretations of generator advantage, limited ranking sensitivity to role reversal, and increased noise from including Qwen2-VL-72B. They identify generator-induced TQA distribution shift as a condition that worsens IRT predictions and explain the subsequent two-model configuration. Cross-release diversity and temporal robustness also receive new interpretation. The original proprietary-model dependence limitation remains.

D1.justification: v3.pdf identifies the previously unspecified blind-test LLM as Llama-3.1-70B, documents additional generator/filter pairings and removal of overlapping biology papers, and changes the code statement from a promised release to availability on GitHub. This is additional disclosure; repository availability was not independently verified. The original prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds Pixtral, Molmo, DOCCI, Ben-Kish et al. on caption hallucinations, and Yanuka et al. on knowledge-adapted captions. The static-benchmark discussion expands slightly, while the positioning against existing live benchmarks and IRT-based efficient evaluation remains substantially unchanged. Related-work passages moved to Appendix A.1 are retained content.

P1.justification: Most existing exposition and the main section sequence remain intact. Changes include moving two related-work discussions into the appendix, reorganizing the efficient-evaluation discussion, distinguishing dataset releases, local wording corrections, and updated author affiliations, publication headers, and acknowledgments. Much of the added length supplies new scientific content rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Table 1 merges separate VQA/TQA blocks into paired columns; Table 4 replaces benchmark averages with individual benchmark columns; Tables 6–7 add ranking columns. New tables and difficulty histograms substantially expand the displays, while longitudinal curves replace the main simulated-split figure. Existing domain plots, generation examples, and prompt templates are redistributed and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Actual successive-release evaluations and generator-bias and temporal-shift studies address important weaknesses of the earlier single-release validation. However, the later paper introduces unresolved numerical conflicts: Table 1's TQA assignments disagree with retained Table 7, and Table 14 reports roughly 56% VQA for LLaVA-1.6-Mistral-7B while Table 16 gives 34.21% for the same dataset release. These affect model comparisons. The PDFs do not establish whether the discrepancies are confined to table preparation or affect the analyses, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
